Helper Functions to Generate MrBayes Blocks in NEXUS Files

mrbayes.Rd

Generates MrBayes command strings for inclusion in a NEXUS MrBayes block. mrbayes_mcmc_cmd(), mrbayes_partition_cmd(), mrbayes_lset_cmd(), mrbayes_prset_cmd(), and mrbayes_sum_cmd() construct individual commands, while mrbayes_block() wraps them in a BEGIN MrBayes; ... END; block. See also prepare_mrbayes_nexus() for an end-to-end wrapper.

Usage

mrbayes_mcmc_cmd(gen = 1e+07, nchains = 4, nruns = 4, stopval = 0.01, ...)

mrbayes_partition_cmd(loci_length, loci_name, protein_coding_loci)

mrbayes_lset_cmd(nst, rates, ..., applyto = NULL)

mrbayes_prset_cmd(..., applyto = NULL)

mrbayes_sum_cmd(..., cmd)

mrbayes_block(...)

Arguments

gen

Numeric or integer. Number of MCMC generations (ngen). Default is 10000000.

nchains

Integer. Number of MCMC chains. Default is 4.

nruns

Integer. Number of parallel runs. Default is 4.

stopval

Numeric. Convergence threshold (stopval) when stoprule = "yes". Default is 0.01.

...

Additional arguments. Must be a named list.

mrbayes_mcmc_cmd()

Further parameters to include in the mcmc command.

mrbayes_lset_cmd()

Further parameters to include in the lset command.

mrbayes_prset_cmd()

Further parameters to include in the prset command.

mrbayes_sum_cmd()

Further parameters to include in sumt or sump; cmd must also be provided to specify "sumt" or "sump".

mrbayes_block()

Commands to include inside the MrBayes block.

loci_length

Numeric vector. Length of each locus.

loci_name

Character vector. Name of each locus.

protein_coding_loci

Character vector. Names of protein-coding loci to partition further by codon position (_pos1, _pos2, _pos3).

nst

Numeric or integer. Value passed to lset nst.

rates

Character. Value passed to lset rates.

applyto

Numeric vector or NULL. Partition indices to apply lset settings to. Default is NULL (applies to the whole alignment).

cmd

Character. Either "sump" or "sumt" when ... arguments are supplied.

Value

A character string containing formatted MrBayes command(s).

See also

prepare_mrbayes_nexus()

Other mrbayes: prepare_mrbayes_nexus()
